clue.text: Break in card game

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to break suddenly and cleanly
second meaning: a children's game of matching cards and calling out

explanation.surface: A pause in play during a hand of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an interval in a game, but the two halves are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a sudden fracture of a stick or bone, and is also the name of a simple matching game with cards.

clue.text: Staff turning up bearing instruction to pay close attention

indicators.note: one piece bears or carries the next, so the parts are simply placed side by side
in a down entry, turning up means the letters climb the column and so read from bottom to top

parts.note: a baton is a short staff or stick

explanation.surface: A member of staff arrives carrying a note telling everyone to listen carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' suggests employees, but it is a stick; 'bearing' does double duty as a compass direction.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase, often abbreviated NB, literally tells a reader to note well and heed what follows.

clue.text: Adventurer provides a means of escape

indicators.note: the longer word supplies the shorter one from within its own letters

parts.note: letters three to six of the word

explanation.surface: An explorer finds a way out of a tight spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A vent is an opening that lets air, smoke or steam out, and figuratively an outlet for feelings.

clue.text: Cross European capital to pick up minstrel's last song

parts.note: cross in the sense of angry

indicators.note: last asks only for the final letter of the possessive word before it

explanation.surface: A wandering minstrel crosses a European city and picks up one final tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like a verb of travel, but it is the adjective meaning angry.
explanation.definitionFit: A madrigal is a part-song for several unaccompanied voices, popular in the sixteenth century.

clue.text: Sign of damage on top of sailor's old lucky charm

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece sitting on top of another simply comes first in the column

parts.note: a scar is the mark left by an injury
AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor's battered old good-luck charm shows the wear of years at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Egyptians carved the dung beetle as an amulet, a talisman believed to bring protection and fortune.

clue.text: Tiny blonde foreign writer

indicators.note: something foreign is strange and unfamiliar, so the letters come out in an unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: A petite fair-haired author from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Enid Blyton was the prolific English children's author of the Famous Five and Noddy books.
explanation.definitionFit: She was a hugely popular twentieth-century British author of children's adventure stories, so she is an example of a writer.

clue.text: Ring taken by Italian robber

indicators.note: the first piece is taken along by the second, so they simply join up in order

parts.note: a band is a ring, as on a finger
standard abbreviation for Italian, as in It vermouth

explanation.surface: A ring is stolen by an Italian thief.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is an outlaw who holds up and steals from travellers, a kind of armed thief.

clue.text: Stop agricultural leader being put in pen

indicators.note: being put in tells us one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its head

explanation.surface: A farm boss is halted and locked in an enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: A pigsty is the farmyard pen, which fits the agricultural surface neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay is to remain or stop where you are, as in stop or stay for dinner.

clue.text: Return promptly with English hangman's equipment

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the word comes back the other way

explanation.surface: An Englishman hurries back with the executioner's rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is the looped rope with a running knot used for execution by hanging.

clue.text: A lad wearing aftershave is going up in the world

indicators.note: a man wearing something has it around him, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: a boy's name, a typical crossword lad

explanation.surface: A young man splashes on cologne and feels he is moving up in society.
explanation.walkthrough: The lad's name Dan goes inside the scent, after the opening A.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascendant describes something rising or gaining power and influence, climbing towards dominance.

clue.text: Tradesperson to re-staple faulty end of spear

indicators.note: something faulty is broken, so the letters are broken up and reassembled
end of asks only for the closing letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A workman is asked to fix a faulty spear point with fresh staples.
explanation.definitionFit: A plasterer is a skilled builder who coats walls and ceilings with smooth plaster, one of the building trades.

clue.text: Theologian featured in Time is child's father

indicators.note: something featured in a show appears inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a day is a period of time
DD, Doctor of Divinity, a theology degree

explanation.surface: A clergyman who appears in Time magazine turns out to be a child's dad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time' with its capital looks like the magazine, but it is just a period of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Daddy is the informal, childlike word for a father, so it is how a child names that parent.

clue.text: Regular gin drunk at sundown

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so the letters reel into a new order

explanation.surface: A regular at the bar downs a gin when the sun sets.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening is the close of the day, the time around sunset and after it.

clue.text: Awfully large composer

indicators.note: done awfully means done badly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A musician who is extremely big.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edward Elgar was the English composer of the Enigma Variations and Pomp and Circumstance marches.

clue.text: Pub gets huge applause for start of something new

indicators.note: the first piece gets or acquires the next, so they are joined in sequence

parts.note: an ovation is enthusiastic sustained clapping

explanation.surface: A bar receives a standing ovation for launching something fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: An innovation is the introduction of a novel method, idea or product, the beginning of a fresh way of doing things.

clue.text: Very happy after start of birth that's overdue

indicators.note: one piece comes after another, fixing the order of the joined parts
start of asks only for the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Parents are overjoyed when a long-awaited baby finally arrives late.
explanation.definitionFit: Belated means coming or happening later than it should have, as with a late birthday card.

clue.text: Opportunity to welcome in new benefactor

indicators.note: to welcome someone in is to admit them inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a door, as in an open door, is an opening or chance

explanation.surface: A chance to bring in a fresh patron.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor is someone who gives money or help to a cause, the same as a benefactor.

clue.text: Part of village about to be let into inside information

indicators.note: something let into a space is admitted inside it

parts.note: gen is British slang for the facts or inside knowledge

explanation.surface: Part of a village is about to be told a secret.
explanation.walkthrough: A village green is the shared grassy space at the heart of an English village.
explanation.definitionFit: The green is the area of common grass in a village, so it is one part of the village.

clue.text: Small dog found in experimentation facility

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a labrador, shortened, which is what 'small' signals

explanation.surface: A little dog turns up in a testing laboratory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small' does not describe the dog's size; it says the breed's name is shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is short both for the labrador retriever breed and for a laboratory where scientific tests are run.

clue.text: Foot of wall lit up in lower part of old Paris prison

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the following word

parts.note: the base is the bottom part

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from bottom to top
the foot of a word in a down entry is its bottom, final letter

explanation.surface: A lamp at the base of a wall lights the dungeon of an old Parisian jail.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed word comes before the final letter of the wall, together going inside the base.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bastille was the Paris fortress-jail stormed in 1789 at the start of the French Revolution.

clue.text: Symbol to know?

parts.note: ken is an old and Scottish verb meaning to know

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the clue splits a word: the verb ken survives in Scots and in the phrase beyond my ken.
explanation.definitionFit: A token is a sign or emblem standing for something else, as in a token of affection.

clue.text: Take me in for treatment with anaesthetic

indicators.note: something given treatment is worked on and altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient asks to be admitted to hospital and put under.
explanation.definitionFit: Ketamine is a drug used in medicine and veterinary practice to induce loss of sensation and consciousness.

clue.text: Practise move before spell of bowling

indicators.note: one piece comes before the other, fixing the order of the joined parts

parts.note: to run is to move quickly
in cricket an over is a set of six balls from one bowler

explanation.surface: A cricketer rehearses a movement before bowling a set of deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a cricket term: six consecutive balls bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: To run over lines or a routine is to rehearse them quickly, going through them for practice.

clue.text: One hundred turned up to meet a railway's legal official

indicators.note: pieces that meet simply join end to end
in a down entry, turned up means the letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: a ton is slang for a hundred

explanation.surface: A hundred people arrive to greet a railway company's lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: A notary is a public officer authorised to witness signatures and certify legal documents.

clue.text: Get back in case of 13 across in wet weather

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the following word
the case of a word is its outer shell, just its first and last letters

parts.note: outer letters of the answer at 13 across

explanation.surface: Recovering a briefcase during an evening downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to EVENING, whose first and last letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: To regain something is to recover it after losing it, so it means to get it back.

clue.text: Spanish fellow takes in visiting politician

indicators.note: to take someone in is to house them inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: señor is the Spanish for a man or mister
visiting someone is being at their place

explanation.surface: A Spanish man puts up a politician who is staying with him.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is an elected member of a senate, a legislative chamber, so is a politician.

clue.text: Choral composition with very small piece for tenor

indicators.note: one piece comes with another, so they are joined side by side

parts.note: a mote is a speck or particle

explanation.surface: A sacred piece of music with a tiny part written for the tenor.
explanation.definitionFit: A motet is a short sacred work for unaccompanied voices, a type of church choir piece.

clue.text: Engage in home shopping

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Take part in buying goods from your sofa.
explanation.definitionFit: Gears mesh or engage when their teeth interlock, so the two verbs share that mechanical sense.

clue.text: Bird exhibited by student entering art examination

indicators.note: something entering goes inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: art in the sense of cunning or craftiness
L, the learner plate, stands for a student
the MOT is Britain's annual roadworthiness test for cars

explanation.surface: An art student shows off a bird drawing in an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' looks like fine art, but it means craftiness here.
explanation.definitionFit: A guillemot is a black-and-white seabird of the auk family that nests on cliff ledges.

clue.text: Tie up Latin master

parts.note: an ace is an expert or master

explanation.surface: Pin down a teacher of Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: To lace shoes or a corset is to fasten them by threading and tying cords.

clue.text: Fish in large barrel on top of aquarium

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece placed on another sits above it, so comes first

parts.note: a tun is a big cask for wine or beer

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down entry is its first letter

explanation.surface: A fish swims in a big barrel standing on a fish tank.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuna is a large ocean food fish of the mackerel family.

clue.text: Tailors are mostly upset by this description of their trade

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective describing the tailors' trade

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word without its final letter

explanation.surface: Tailors are mostly annoyed by the way their craft is described.
explanation.definitionFit: Sartorial is the adjective for tailoring and clothes, from the Latin sartor, a tailor.

clue.text: Conservative welcoming a new member of the clergy

indicators.note: welcoming someone means taking them in, so one piece goes inside another

explanation.surface: A Tory greets a newly arrived clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a priest attached to a cathedral chapter, so is one of the clergy.
